timeouts.ceilingsDescription: Bound the resource and timeout overrides $t(terms:project.pluralLower) and environments can configure
timeouts.ceilingsIntro: — anyone who can edit a $t(terms:project.singularLower) or environment's Deployment Config can override them, including overriding them to unlimited. These ceilings bound those overrides. All three are off by default, so nothing changes until you set one, and holders of the Settings write permission are never blocked by them. An override that breaks a ceiling is rejected with an explanation, never silently reduced.
timeouts.ceilingsRetro: Setting a ceiling here does not change $t(terms:project.pluralLower) that already exceed it — they keep running as configured until someone next edits them. Note also that the memory ceiling is per container, so a $t(terms:project.singularLower) with several replicas can still total more than the ceiling.
timeouts.memoryHint: 0 = no ceiling (default). When set, a $t(terms:project.singularLower) cannot request more than this, nor set its memory limit to unlimited.
timeouts.allowUnlimitedHint: On by default. Turn it off to stop a $t(terms:project.singularLower) from setting its request, SSE, or WebSocket timeout to 0 — the value that opts out of the hard ceiling above entirely. Timeouts a $t(terms:project.singularLower) sets to a real number are already clamped to that ceiling.
